name: demo-deep-think
description: Demo "Thinking": a discovery run (OCR fallback for handwritten claim forms) dominated by long streaming thinking pauses of 2-5 minutes, with occasional reads; declares 2 phases / 3 tasks and closes them with diff and test evidence (~28 minutes).

steps.thinking: Handwritten claim forms defeat the printed-text OCR engine. Before planning: how is OCR routed today, what confidence do we get on handwriting, and what is the cheapest safe fallback?

steps.text: Reading how OCR is routed today before I plan anything.

steps.thinking: Two options: always run both engines (double cost), or gate the handwriting engine on low printed-text confidence. Gating is cheaper and keeps latency for printed forms.

args.summary: Confidence-gated OCR fallback for handwritten claim forms.

tasks.title: Compare OCR engines on handwritten samples
Prototype the confidence-gated fallback router
tasks.acceptance: Forms below 0.6 printed-text confidence go to the handwriting engine

input.content:
# OCR engines on handwritten claim forms

<!-- build {{sim.sessionId}} -->

| Engine | Printed forms | Handwritten forms | p95 latency |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| print-ocr | 0.97 | 0.41 | 0.8 s |
| hand-ocr | 0.88 | 0.83 | 2.9 s |

Handwriting accuracy needs the second engine; printed forms do not.

steps.thinking: Threshold choice: 0.6 keeps 92% of printed forms on the fast path in the sample set while catching every handwritten form below 0.5.

input.content:
# Confidence-gated OCR fallback

<!-- build {{sim.sessionId}} -->

- Run print-ocr first (fast path).
- Below 0.6 page confidence, re-run the page on hand-ocr and keep the higher-confidence result.
- Record which engine produced every field so adjusters can see it.
- Cost: +18% OCR spend on the sample mix, versus +100% for always running both.

evidence.ref: test/ocr/router.test.ts > falls back to the handwriting engine below 0.6 confidence

steps.text: The OCR fallback is designed and prototyped: print-ocr first, hand-ocr below 0.6 confidence.
